NIKL’s report covers null arguments and antecedent recovery, but no exact locator here distinguishes Korean subject/object nulls from topic/anaphora for each example in the article. The taxonomy claim is only partial.

Fuentes revisadas en este seguimiento: Effects of Discourse Factors on the Interpretation of Korean Null Pronouns in Subject and Object Position — Abstract, article pp. 655–669 (2020), especially statement that interpretation of null pronouns in subject/object position is affected by discourse cues, coherence relations and syntactic cues. Resultado: Experimental research supports discourse-sensitive interpretation of null pronouns in subject/object positions; it does not warrant all pedagogical examples or absolute recoverability claims.
The syntax of Korean anaphora: An experimental investigation — Dissertation (2019), PDF lines 1051–1055 on Korean subject/object arguments being omissible and recovered; chapter on null objects, lines 5895–5949. Resultado: Primary dissertation research supports Korean argument omission and context-sensitive null-object interpretation; it does not validate all sample sentences and pragmatic generalizations.
